context: Streamlines the login route, dropping a middleware that a contributor flagged as 'probably unused'.
explanation: The rate limiter guarding /login was removed entirely, so the endpoint now accepts unlimited login attempts from any client. That turns it into an open door for credential-stuffing and brute-force password guessing. Fix: keep (or reinstate) per-IP/per-account rate limiting on all authentication endpoints, ideally paired with account lockout or backoff after repeated failures.
